subject: SDLC artifacts: branch policy, CI approvals & ephemeral key rotation — SIG follow-up
messages:
From: Brightline Audit <brightline-audit@example.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: artifacts for SIG review — branch policy, CI approvals, key rotation

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking this on. For the SIG assessment we're putting together a compact evidence bundle focused on Secure SDLC controls. Specifically we need:  
- Current enforced branch protection settings (including who can merge, required reviews, status checks). 
- CI/CD approval records for protected branches (logs showing approver, timestamps, PR id).
- Evidence that deployment keys (or machine/service keys) are ephemeral or rotated on a schedule (rotation dates + where rotation is logged).
- An inventory of any service accounts with long-lived credentials in the repo environment (if none, say so).

Can you provide a short narrative + the artifacts (PDF/CSV/MD) by EOD Wednesday? If some items require redaction, mark them and we'll coordinate a secure transfer.

Also: please include an auditable trail showing when change approvals last occurred (can be a CSV export).

Thanks,
Samira Patel
Senior Assessor — Brightline

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Brightline Audit <brightline-audit@example.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: artifacts for SIG review — branch policy, CI approvals, key rotation

Hi Samira,

Acknowledged — we'll assemble a compact bundle. Quick notes:  
- Attaching a PDF snapshot of the branch protection settings exported from our SCM admin console (branch-protection-snapshot-20260829.pdf). It shows required approvals, required status checks, and the list of admin overrides.
- We're including a CSV export of CI approval events for PR merges to main and release/* from 2026-06-01 through 2026-08-31 (ci-approval-logs-202606-202608.csv). Sensitive columns (internal user IDs) are redacted per our policy; the CSV includes approver email, PR id, timestamp, approval type.
- Mina will add the secrets rotation summary and confirm rotation cadence for deploy keys.

Questions: do you need the raw commit SHAs included in the CSV, or is PR id + merge timestamp sufficient for your review?

I'll drop these in a restricted Drive folder and can provide a signed DocuSign/ticket link if required.

Best,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Security Liaison — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: artifacts for SIG review — branch policy, CI approvals, key rotation

Logan — good start, I've reviewed the exports. A couple operational clarifications to include before we hand off:
- The branch snapshot shows that the "release/*" pattern requires at least two reviewers and the CI status check named "pipeline/integration" is required. Please call out the escalation path for emergency merges (we log overrides in the admin audit).
- For the CI CSV: include one additional column we maintain called "approval_source" (UI vs API). That helps prove approvals weren't auto-approved via automation. I've attached a sanitized extract I generated (ci-approval-logs-202606-202608.csv).
- Add a short note (1-2 lines) describing our PR gating policy and how we handle approver conflicts.

Attachment: deploy-key-ephemeral-policy.txt (policy excerpt describing ephemeral deploy keys for staging/prod; includes TTL semantics).

I'll also add the internal drive link to the package. Rishi — can you confirm that we don't have any long-lived repo-scoped service credentials outside of the KMS-wrapped keys?

Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Security — Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: artifacts for SIG review — branch policy, CI approvals, key rotation

Thanks — adding the secrets rotation summary. High-level points to include in the narrative:
- All deployment keys used by our CI runners are issued from a short-lived certificate authority and rotated on a 30-day cadence. Rotation events are recorded in our secret-management audit log (see attached secrets_rotation_summary_2026-08.md).
- KMS keys: primary KMS key IDs are redacted in the artifact; auditors can request view-only access if they need full identifiers.
- No long-lived plaintext credentials are stored in repositories; any legacy service token was retired 2025-11-12 (ticket RED-804).

Attachment: secrets_rotation_summary_2026-08.md (includes table of rotation events, ticket links, and log export IDs).

Mina Haddad
Manager, Infrastructure Security — Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Brightline Audit <brightline-audit@example.com>, Acme Security <security@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Final delivery: SDLC artifacts for SIG review (branch policy, CI approvals, key rotation)

Hi Samira / Acme security team,

We've uploaded the requested artifacts to a restricted Drive folder and attached sanitized exports to this thread: branch-protection-snapshot-20260829.pdf, ci-approval-logs-202606-202608.csv, secrets_rotation_summary_2026-08.md, deploy-key-ephemeral-policy.txt.  

For quick reference:  
- Branch protection: required approvals and required status checks are enforced for main and release/*; emergency override events are captured (admin audit).
- CI approvals: CSV includes approver email, PR id, timestamp, approval_source (UI/API). Raw commit SHAs are available on request under controlled access.
- Keys: deploy keys are ephemeral (30-day TTL), rotation events logged in secret-management audit IDs (see file). No long-lived repo credentials remain.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-branch-policy
HubSpot record: HBSP-45321
Internal CI logs (read-only): https://logs.internal.redwood.example/ci/approvals?range=2026-06-01_2026-08-31

If you'd like a short walkthrough, Marissa or Mina can join a 20-min call tomorrow morning. Otherwise please confirm receipt and whether any items need redaction or expanded logs.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Security Liaison — Redwood Inference
